plain_words.what: We decided who owns what, and how many separate things get deployed.
plain_words.decided: One person owns everything. Two deployables: the app (subscriptions and billing together) and the warehouse.
plain_words.assumed: Subscriptions and billing can live in one app. They change together and one person runs both.
plain_words.riskiest: That pairing is why one message below needs no contract. Split them later and it becomes a real seam that does.

deployables.name: Warehouse service
deployables.rationale: Runs on the warehouse network with different uptime/latency needs than the customer app; integrated by async events (week-charged) so the app never blocks on it

scale_check.note: 2 of a 1–3 target: fulfilment runs on the warehouse network with different uptime needs (understand C1 / hotspot H1), so it is split; billing stays in the app as a Stripe adapter. Why not fewer: on-site runtime. Why not more: one team, no scaling evidence.

decisions.question: One modular monolith or split the warehouse service now?

options.summary: One modular monolith now; fulfilment is a module reached from the warehouse over the network.
pros: One deploy, one database, one log to read at 2am
Nothing to split until a real runtime constraint shows up
cons: A cloud outage stops packing on the warehouse floor
Warehouse latency and uptime needs are ignored until they bite
risks: The fulfilment module quietly reaches into subscription tables and the seam disappears

options.summary: Split the warehouse service now so packing runs on the warehouse network.
pros: Packing keeps working when the cloud link drops
Fulfilment can deploy on the warehouse schedule, not the app schedule
cons: Two deploys and two data stores for one person
week-charged needs a real contract and an outbox from day one
risks: Distributed failure modes (duplicate box-packed, lost events) arrive before the business has a second site

options.summary: One modular monolith with a warehouse module boundary enforced by a fitness test, split when the runtime need is proven.
pros: Cheapest now; the split stays possible because the test keeps the seam clean
The decision waits for evidence instead of guessing
cons: Still one runtime, so the outage problem is only deferred
Someone must keep the fitness test honest
risks: The test passes while the shared database still couples the modules underneath

would_flip_if: The warehouse network is proven unreliable enough that packing must survive a cloud outage
A second warehouse or a packing partner appears and needs its own deploy
The founder hires a second developer who can carry a separate service
